title: one-step equations with whole-number coefficients and solutions

lesson.title: Balance It Out: Solving One-Step Equations

steps.say: Hi friend, it's Ms. Yuanyuan! Imagine you go to the corner store in Vancouver and buy one hot chocolate. You hand over your money, and the change tells you it cost some amount, but the price tag fell off. You know your snack plus three dollars for a muffin came to eleven dollars all together. That mystery price is what we call a variable, and we usually write it as the letter x. Today we learn how to find that mystery number.

visual.caption: The two small bars together must match the total of eleven dollars

steps.say: Here is the big idea. An equation is like a balance scale, the kind you might see in science class. The equals sign in the middle means both sides weigh exactly the same. On the left we have x plus three, and on the right we have eleven. The scale is perfectly level, so whatever x is, the two sides match.

visual.caption: Balanced: both sides weigh the same

steps.say: Now here is the golden rule, and it is the only rule you really need. It is called preserving equality. If I take three kilograms off the left pan, I must take three kilograms off the right pan too. Do the same thing to both sides and the scale stays level. If I only took some off one side, it would tip over and the equation would no longer be true.

visual.caption: Take three off both sides, and it stays level

steps.say: Let's finish it. On the left, three plus three take away three leaves just x sitting alone. On the right, eleven take away three is eight. So x equals eight. The hot chocolate cost eight dollars. Now let's check, because checking is what good mathematicians do. Eight plus three is eleven. It works!

visual.caption: x sits alone on the left, and it equals eight

steps.say: Now a slightly different one. Suppose you and two friends share a bag of clementines equally, so three equal groups, and the whole bag has twelve clementines. We write that as three times x equals twelve. Here the three is not being added, it is telling us we have three equal groups of x.

visual.caption: Three equal groups, twelve clementines in total

steps.say: Since three groups make twelve, we undo the multiplying by dividing. And remember the golden rule, do it to both sides. Divide the left by three and divide the right by three. Three x divided by three leaves one x, and twelve divided by three is four. So x equals four. Each friend gets four clementines. Let's check: three times four is twelve. Perfect.

visual.caption: Three equal bars of four make twelve

steps.say: So notice the pattern. If something was added to x, you subtract it from both sides. If x was multiplied by something, you divide both sides. You always do the opposite operation, and you always do it to both sides, so the scale never tips.

visual.caption: Subtract five from both sides: x equals six

steps.say: And that is it! Keep the scale balanced, undo with the opposite operation, and always check your answer by putting your number back in. You did wonderfully today.

lesson.answer: Whatever you do to one side of the equation, do the very same thing to the other side — then undo with the opposite operation to set x free.

practice.question: Maya buys 4 identical reusable water bottles at the store in Kelowna and the total is 32 dollars. If x is the price of one bottle, the equation is 4x = 32. What is x? Then try this one: a plank of wood is x centimetres long, and after Dad adds a 7 centimetre piece the total is 25 centimetres. Solve x + 7 = 25.
practice.answer: For 4x = 32, divide both sides by 4: x = 8, so each bottle costs 8 dollars (check: 4 × 8 = 32). For x + 7 = 25, subtract 7 from both sides: x = 18, so the plank is 18 centimetres long (check: 18 + 7 = 25).
